claim: MCP versioning page: 'The current protocol version is 2026-07-28'; 2025-11-25 and earlier are the handshake-based revisions.

MCP 2026-07-28 removes protocol-level sessions (Mcp-Session-Id) and the initialize handshake; every request carries version and capabilities in _meta; servers MUST implement server/discover; tasks move to the extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks; Multi Round-Trip Requests replace server-initiated requests (roots, sampling, elicitation); SSE resumability removed.

MCP 2026-07-28 deprecates Roots, Sampling and Logging and deprecates OAuth Dynamic Client Registration; it documents OpenTelemetry trace context (traceparent, tracestate, baggage) in _meta (SEP-414) and asks servers to return tools/list in a deterministic order.

MCP 2026-07-28 authorization: MCP servers MUST implement RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata; MCP clients MUST implement RFC 8707 resource indicators using the server's canonical URI; servers MUST validate that tokens were issued for them as audience; authorization servers and clients SHOULD support Client ID Metadata Documents.

MCP elicitation: servers MUST NOT use form mode to request passwords, API keys, access tokens or payment credentials and MUST use URL mode for them; URL mode (introduced 2025-11-25) sends the user to an external URL so the interaction does not pass through the MCP client.

The official MCP Registry is in preview ('breaking changes or data resets may occur'), does not support private servers, and its codebase is not designed for self-hosting; private registries may implement its API to benefit from host support.

MCP extensions status table: OAuth Client Credentials Stable; Enterprise-Managed Authorization Stable; MCP Apps (interactive UI) Stable; MCP Tasks 'Beta, to Core'; Skills over MCP Beta; Server Cards Beta.
MCP governance: contributions are Apache-2.0; Lead Maintainers (BDFL) hold final decision authority; membership is for individuals, not companies.

The Linux Foundation announced the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) on 2025-12-09 with founding contributions MCP (Anthropic), goose (Block) and AGENTS.md (OpenAI); Platinum members include AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI.
MCP SDK tiers: TypeScript, Python, C#, Go, Rust and Ruby are Tier 1; Java Tier 2; Swift, PHP and Kotlin Tier 3; 'SDKs adopt new protocol revisions on their own schedules'.
MCP Python SDK main lists MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = ('2026-07-28',) and its 2026-07-28 conformance expected-failures baseline is empty for client and server.
MCP TypeScript SDK main defines FIRST_MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2026-07-28'; MCP Go SDK main runs conformance with --requirements 2026-07-28.

claim: Home Assistant's MCP server integration implements OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and supports Client ID Metadata Documents; the main URL /api/mcp requires an administrator and exposes all tool sets by default; a read-only option exists; the Device control tool set only reaches entities exposed to voice assistants.

Backstage MCP Actions: action attributes default conservatively (non-idempotent, not read-only, destructive unless readOnly); tool names are namespaced by plugin ID; named servers filter actions by glob include/exclude rules, while the default server /api/mcp-actions/v1 always exposes every action.

Olares CLI ships 12 Agent Skills (olares-shared, chart, files, market, settings, dashboard, cluster, doctor, router, knowledge, search, publish); released bundles are compiled into the CLI binary (go:embed of olares-*/SKILL.md), installed to ~/.agents/skills and linked into Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw skill folders.
Olares (AGPL-3.0) has no OS-level MCP server in its main repository: a git grep for MCP terms matched only documentation use-case pages.

umbrelOS 2.1.0-beta.1 MCP server: tools are registered from five files; the 4 system-info tools are always registered, system-management tools (7, including install_os_update and restart_device) only when manageSystem is granted; there are 38 registerTool call sites in total (37 literal tool names plus one loop-registered name).
umbrelOS 2.1.0-beta.1 keeps the connecting agent's self-declared identity and lastRequestAt in memory only; no persistent per-call audit record was found in the MCP module.

Agent Skills specification: a skill is a folder with SKILL.md; YAML frontmatter requires name (max 64 chars, lowercase, digits, hyphens) and description (max 1024 chars); optional license, compatibility (max 500 chars) and experimental allowed-tools.

claim: GDPR Art. 4(14) defines biometric data (e.g. facial images, dactyloscopic data) and Art. 9(1) prohibits processing biometric data 'for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person' unless an Art. 9(2) exception applies (e.g. explicit consent).

GDPR Art. 2(2)(c) excludes processing 'by a natural person in the course of a purely personal or household activity'; Recital 18 adds that the Regulation 'applies to controllers or processors which provide the means for processing personal data for such personal or household activities'.

COPPA Rule 16 CFR 312.2, as amended at 90 FR 16977 (2025-04-22): 'personal information' includes 'a biometric identifier that can be used for the automated or semi-automated recognition of an individual, such as fingerprints; ... voiceprints; gait patterns; facial templates; or faceprints'.

Washington RCW 19.375.020: a person may not enroll a biometric identifier in a database for a commercial purpose without notice, consent, or a mechanism to prevent later commercial use; 'enroll' means capture, convert to a template and store it matched to an individual.

EU AI Act Art. 2(10): the Regulation 'does not apply to obligations of deployers who are natural persons using AI systems in the course of a purely personal non-professional activity'; Art. 5(1) prohibits untargeted scraping of facial images to build recognition databases and biometric categorisation inferring race, politics, religion, sex life or orientation (Chapters I-II apply from 2 February 2025).

EU AI Act Annex III point 1 lists as high-risk: remote biometric identification (excluding verification 'the sole purpose of which is to confirm that a specific natural person is the person he or she claims to be'), biometric categorisation by sensitive attributes, and emotion recognition.

Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026 (Digital Omnibus on AI) moves the application of Chapter III Sections 1-3 to 2 December 2027 for Annex III high-risk systems and to 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems; it enters into force on the third day after publication.

W3C Web Authentication Level 3 is a W3C Recommendation dated 25 August 2026; §14.3: biometric recognition happens inside the authenticator and 'Biometric data is not revealed to the WebAuthn Relying Party'.
